advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the exit-code->annotation MAPPING (exit 2 within the `2)`/unreachable arm, exit 1 within the `1)`/divergence arm), not bare substring presence anywhere in the run block.
evidence: tests/unit/test_mirror_guard_workflow.py:26-31: `assert 'case "$code" in' in run` ... `assert "exit 2" in run` ... `assert "exit 1" in run`
The assertions use `in run` (substring anywhere in the whole block), so `exit 1` and `exit 2` are not tied to their respective case arms (mirror-guard.yml:63-72 `1)` -> exit 1 / `2)` -> exit 2).
Regression-blindness: a diff that swapped the exit codes between the divergence and unreachable arms leaves every asserted substring present, so this test cannot fail on that regression.

These strings are prose inside `echo ...::error title=...` / step-summary text (mirror-guard.yml:69-70); no non-human consumer branches on the exact wording, so re-wording the operator message with identical behavior would break the test.
advisory.finding: The workflow test only presence-checks substrings anywhere in the shell body and never verifies the exit-code->annotation MAPPING the diff introduces; a regression that swaps the case arms (e.g. emitting 'exit 2'/'unreachable' under the `1)` divergence arm and 'exit 1'/'divergence' under the `2)` arm) would still contain all six substrings and pass, so the test is blind to the exact 'unreachable distinct from divergence' behavior it claims to guard.
merged_from: Two workflow-test assertions pin author-facing prose rather than a machine-consumed contract, making them change-detectors that break on a harmless wording change with no behavior change.
advisory.suggested_fix: Parse the `case` arms (or shellcheck-exercise them with a stubbed `python -m rebar.mirror_guard` that returns each code) and assert that code 2 produces the 'unreachable' annotation and exit 2, and code 1 produces the 'divergence' annotation and exit 1.
